title: 2 Kings Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 25.

questions.question: In which year of King Zedekiah's reign did Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come against Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Ninth year
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:1 states that Nebuchadnezzar came in the ninth year of King Zedekiah's reign.

questions.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar and his host do when they came against Jerusalem?
options: Pitched against it and built forts round about
Entered the city and captured the king
Made peace with the city elders
questions.correctAnswer: Pitched against it and built forts round about
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:1 explains that Nebuchadnezzar and his host pitched against Jerusalem and built forts around it.

questions.question: How long was Jerusalem besieged according to 2 Kings 25?
options: Until the ninth year of King Zedekiah
Until the tenth year of King Zedekiah
Until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah
Until the twelfth year of King Zedekiah
questions.correctAnswer: Until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:2 states the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

questions.question: On what day did the famine prevail in Jerusalem, causing no bread for the people?
options: Ninth day of the fourth month
Tenth day of the tenth month
Seventh day of the fifth month
Twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month
questions.correctAnswer: Ninth day of the fourth month
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:3 records the famine prevailing on the ninth day of the fourth month.

questions.question: How did the men of war escape the city when it was broken up?
options: By night through the gate between two walls by the king's garden
By day through the main gate
By tunneling under the city walls
questions.correctAnswer: By night through the gate between two walls by the king's garden
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:4 states the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls near the king's garden.

questions.question: Where was King Zedekiah overtaken by the Chaldees?
questions.correctAnswer: In the plains of Jericho
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:5 says the army of the Chaldees overtook the king in the plains of Jericho.

questions.question: What happened to Zedekiah's sons before his eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: They were slain
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:7 records that Zedekiah's sons were slain before his eyes.

questions.question: What was done to Zedekiah after his sons were slain?
options: His eyes were put out and he was bound with brass fetters
He was crowned king in Babylon
He was made captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: His eyes were put out and he was bound with brass fetters
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:7 explains that Zedekiah's eyes were put out and he was bound with brass fetters.

questions.question: Who came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, on the seventh day, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year?
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:8 states that Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, came at that time.

questions.question: What did Nebuzaradan do to the house of the LORD and the king's house?
options: He converted them into a palace
questions.correctAnswer: He burnt them with fire
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:9 records that Nebuzaradan burnt the house of the LORD and the king's house with fire.

questions.question: True or False: The army of the Chaldees broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:10 states the army of the Chaldees broke down Jerusalem's walls round about.

questions.question: True or False: The city was besieged during the twelfth year of King Zedekiah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:2 shows the city was besieged until the eleventh year, not the twelfth year of Zedekiah.

questions.question: True or False: The men of war fled by day through the gate near the king's garden.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:4 specifies the men of war fled by night, not by day.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuzaradan was a servant of the king of Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:8 describes Nebuzaradan as a servant of the king of Babylon.

questions.question: Which event happened first in 2 Kings 25?
options: The city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah
The famine prevailed in the city
Zedekiah fled the city by night
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadnezzar built forts around Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:1 records Nebuchadnezzar pitching against Jerusalem and building forts before the siege (verse 2) and famine (verse 3) and Zedekiah's flight (verse 4).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carry away from Jerusalem?
options: The rest of the people left in the city, fugitives, and the remnant of the multitude
Only the king and his family
questions.correctAnswer: The rest of the people left in the city, fugitives, and the remnant of the multitude
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:11 states that Nebuzaradan carried away the rest of the people left in the city, the fugitives who fell away to the king of Babylon, along with the remnant of the multitude, while verse 12 indicates the poor were left behind.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 25, what role were the poor of the land left to perform?
questions.correctAnswer: Vinedressers and husbandmen
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:12 clearly states that the captain of the guard left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, indicating they were kept to work the land.

questions.question: What did the Chaldees do to the brass pillars and bases that were in the house of the LORD?
options: They broke them in pieces and carried the brass to Babylon
They melted them down to make weapons
They left them intact as a sign of respect
They buried them under the temple ruins
questions.correctAnswer: They broke them in pieces and carried the brass to Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:13 explains that the Chaldees broke the brass pillars and bases in pieces and took the brass to Babylon, showing the destruction and plundering of the temple treasures.

questions.question: Which items did the captain of the guard take away from the temple that were used in ministry?
options: Pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all brass vessels
questions.correctAnswer: Pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all brass vessels
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 25:14, the captain of the guard took away pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all vessels of brass used in ministering, indicating comprehensive removal of temple service items.

questions.question: What precious metals did the captain of the guard seize besides brass vessels?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold and silver items
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:15 states that the captain of the guard took firepans, bowls, and other such things made of gold and silver, showing that valuable treasures were also taken.

questions.question: What is described about the two pillars Solomon made for the house of the LORD?
options: One pillar was eighteen cubits high with a brass chapiter three cubits high, adorned with wreathen work and pomegranates
Both pillars were made of pure gold
The pillars were hidden before the siege
They were destroyed by fire before being taken
questions.correctAnswer: One pillar was eighteen cubits high with a brass chapiter three cubits high, adorned with wreathen work and pomegranates
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:16-17 describe the height and ornamentation of the pillars Solomon made, indicating their grandeur and craftsmanship.

questions.question: Who were taken by the captain of the guard from among the priests and temple officials?
options: Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three keepers of the door
questions.correctAnswer: Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three keepers of the door
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:18 specifies these particular priests and temple officials were taken by the captain of the guard, highlighting key religious leaders being captured.

questions.question: Which group of people was taken out of the city together with an officer over the men of war?
options: Five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and sixty men of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and sixty men of the people
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:19 describes the capture of an officer over the men of war, five men who were in the king's presence, the principal scribe, and sixty men, indicating the removal of leadership and military officials.

questions.question: What happened to those taken by Nebuzaradan to the king of Babylon at Riblah?
options: They were smitten and slain by the king of Babylon
They were released after paying tribute
They were made governors in exile
They were kept as envoys to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They were smitten and slain by the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:21 states that the king of Babylon smote and slew those taken to Riblah, showing the harsh judgment on Judah's leaders.

questions.question: Who was made ruler over the people remaining in the land of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar?
questions.correctAnswer: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:22 indicates Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah as ruler over the remnant in Judah, showing Babylon's attempt to maintain control through a local governor.

questions.question: What did Gedaliah promise those who served the king of Babylon and dwelt in the land?
options: It shall be well with you
You will be given riches and fame
You will be taken to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be well with you
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 25:24, Gedaliah swore to the captains and their men that if they feared not serving the Chaldees and dwelt in the land, it would go well with them, encouraging submission for peace.

questions.question: True or False: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah killed Gedaliah and others at Mizpah, causing fear among the people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:25 records that Ishmael killed Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldees with him at Mizpah, which led to fear among the people as described in verse 26.

questions.question: What did the people and captains do after Gedaliah was slain and they feared the Chaldees?
options: They arose and went to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They arose and went to Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:26 states that fearing the Chaldees, all the people, small and great, and the captains arose and went to Egypt, seeking safety outside their land.

questions.question: How does the restoration of Jehoiachin in Babylon teach about God's providence and mercy?
options: Evilmerodach lifted Jehoiachin from prison, spoke kindly to him, and provided for him continually
Jehoiachin escaped from prison by his own strength
Jehoiachin was forgotten and died in prison
Jehoiachin was made king again in Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Evilmerodach lifted Jehoiachin from prison, spoke kindly to him, and provided for him continually
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:27-30 shows that after 37 years of captivity, Jehoiachin was treated kindly by the Babylonian king, demonstrating God's sovereignty and mercy even in exile.

questions.question: True or False: The brass of the vessels taken from the temple was weighed before being taken to Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:16 specifies that the brass of all these vessels was without weight, meaning it was not weighed before being taken, indicating the vast quantity or disregard for precise accounting.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 25.

questions.question: Where were the people that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away from Jerusalem taken?
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:11 states that Nebuzaradan carried away the rest of the people left in Jerusalem, which historically refers to their exile to Babylon, consistent with other exiles in 2 Kings 25 and Jeremiah 52.

questions.question: Who was made ruler over the people that remained in the land of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar?
questions.correctAnswer: Gedaliah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:22 specifies that Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam as ruler over the remnant in Judah to govern after the exile.

questions.question: Which city did Gedaliah govern after being appointed by the king of Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:23 shows that Gedaliah was at Mizpah when the captains and their men came to him, indicating his governance base there.

questions.question: What did Gedaliah promise those who came to him regarding serving the Chaldees?
options: Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:24 records Gedaliah's oath encouraging people to serve the Chaldees and live peacefully in the land, promising them well-being.

questions.question: Who killed Gedaliah, causing further unrest among the remnant in Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:25 tells us that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, of royal seed, came with ten men and assassinated Gedaliah at Mizpah.

questions.question: What did the people do after the assassination of Gedaliah according to 2 Kings 25:26?
questions.correctAnswer: Fled to Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:26 states that the people, including captains and small and great, fled to Egypt out of fear of the Chaldees after Gedaliah's death.

questions.question: How many years into Jehoiachin’s captivity was he released from prison by Evilmerodach?
questions.correctAnswer: 37 years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:27 clearly states it was in the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin’s captivity that Evilmerodach released him from prison.

questions.question: What honor did Evilmerodach bestow upon Jehoiachin upon his release?
options: Set his throne above the kings in Babylon
Made him captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: Set his throne above the kings in Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:28 states Evilmerodach set Jehoiachin’s throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon, a sign of honor and restoration.

questions.question: True or False: After being released, Jehoiachin was executed by Evilmerodach.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:29-30 show that Jehoiachin was treated kindly, given new garments, ate regularly before the king, and received a continual allowance, indicating he was not executed.

questions.question: True or False: The assassination of Gedaliah led to the remnant fleeing to Egypt out of fear of the Chaldees.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:25-26 describes that after Gedaliah was killed by Ishmael, the people fled to Egypt because they feared the Chaldees.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the narrative structure of 2 Kings 25, showing the fall of Jerusalem and the exile followed by restoration of Jehoiachin?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with Jerusalem’s destruction and exile, and ends with Jehoiachin’s release and favor in Babylon, framing the narrative with an inclusio structure, highlighting fall and restoration (2 Kings 25:1 and 25:27-30).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage is closely connected to the destruction described in 2 Kings 25, especially the burning of the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 52
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 52 recounts events parallel to 2 Kings 25, including the siege of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple by Nebuchadnezzar, showing a historical and thematic connection.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as “captain of the guard” in this chapter is "Nebuzaradan". What is the likely meaning of this title in the ancient Near Eastern context?
questions.correctAnswer: Commander of the royal guard
questions.explanation: The title 'captain of the guard' (Hebrew: 'seren ha-patalim') refers to a military commander in charge of the king’s elite troops, consistent with Nebuzaradan’s role overseeing the destruction and exile (2 Kings 25:8).

questions.question: Which theme from 2 Kings 25 is echoed in the New Testament regarding restoration and forgiveness?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus forgiving and restoring sinners (Luke 15)
questions.explanation: The theme of restoration after exile in 2 Kings 25, especially Jehoiachin’s release, parallels Luke 15’s message of forgiveness and restoration, where lost ones are accepted back with favor (2 Kings 25:27-30 and Luke 15).

questions.question: What was done to the pillars, bases, and the brasen sea in Solomon’s temple by the Chaldees?
options: They broke them in pieces and carried the brass to Babylon
They melted them down to make weapons
They buried them under the temple ruins
questions.correctAnswer: They broke them in pieces and carried the brass to Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:13 describes how the Chaldees broke the brass pillars, bases, and sea in pieces and took the brass to Babylon, symbolizing the desecration and removal of the temple’s glory.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the captivity and judgment of King Zedekiah as described in 2 Kings 25:6-7?
options: Divine justice and judgment for sin
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice and judgment for sin
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 show that Nebuchadnezzar brought judgment upon King Zedekiah, executing his sons and blinding him, demonstrating God's righteous judgment against unrepentant sin (2 Kings 25:6-7). This aligns with the doctrine of divine justice (Romans 2:5-6).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in Nebuzaradan’s burning of the temple and king’s house in 2 Kings 25:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness and righteous wrath
questions.explanation: The burning of the LORD’s house and king’s house by Nebuzaradan illustrates God's holiness and His righteous wrath against idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness (2 Kings 25:9). This reflects God’s intolerance of sin (Isaiah 6:3).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 25:12 demonstrate God's providential care amid judgment?
options: By sparing the poor to cultivate the land
By sending a prophet to comfort the exiles
By destroying all inhabitants without exception
questions.correctAnswer: By sparing the poor to cultivate the land
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows that the captain of the guard left some poor people to be vinedressers and husbandmen, indicating God's providential care to preserve life and the possibility of future restoration even amid judgment (2 Kings 25:12).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is taught by 2 Kings 25:13-16 regarding the destruction of Solomon’s temple vessels?
options: The judgment of God extends to sacred things, signifying the seriousness of covenant breach
The vessels were worthless and easily discarded
The temple was made of impermanent materials
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment of God extends to sacred things, signifying the seriousness of covenant breach
questions.explanation: Verses 13-16 describe the breaking and carrying away of the brass pillars and temple vessels Solomon made, symbolizing that even holy objects are subject to judgment when covenant faithfulness is broken (2 Kings 25:13-16). This underscores God's holiness and justice (Exodus 25:10-22).

questions.question: What does the fate of the chief priests and officials taken to Riblah in 2 Kings 25:18-21 reveal about God's judgment on leadership?
options: God holds leaders accountable for the nation's sins
God prefers military leaders over priests
God judges only the people, not their leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God holds leaders accountable for the nation's sins
questions.explanation: The capture and execution of the chief priest and officials at Riblah in verses 18-21 shows that God holds leadership responsible for the people's sins and failures (2 Kings 25:18-21), reflecting biblical teaching on leadership accountability (Ezekiel 34:4).

questions.question: How does Gedaliah’s appointment as governor over the remnant in 2 Kings 25:22-24 illustrate God’s providential governance?
options: God provides leadership for His people even in exile
God immediately restores the kingdom to its former glory
questions.correctAnswer: God provides leadership for His people even in exile
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show Nebuchadnezzar appointing Gedaliah over those left in the land, demonstrating God's providence in preserving order and governance for His people despite judgment (2 Kings 25:22-24). This reflects God's sustaining care (Psalm 78:72).

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining 2 Kings 25:25 and 26 concerning human response to divine judgment?
options: Fear of judgment leads to flight and rejection of God's appointed leaders
Repentance and submission to God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of judgment leads to flight and rejection of God's appointed leaders
questions.explanation: Verse 25 records Ishmael killing Gedaliah, and verse 26 describes the people fleeing to Egypt out of fear of the Chaldeans, illustrating how fear of divine judgment can provoke rejection of God’s appointed governance and lead to further disobedience (2 Kings 25:25-26).

questions.question: What attribute of God is manifested in the restoration of Jehoiachin’s status in captivity as described in 2 Kings 25:27-30?
options: God’s mercy and faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Verses 27-30 describe Evil-merodach lifting Jehoiachin from prison and treating him kindly, which shows God’s mercy and faithfulness to His covenant, preserving a remnant and hope for restoration (2 Kings 25:27-30). This reflects God's covenantal mercy (Lamentations 3:22-23).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 25:1-2 fit into the broader redemptive narrative of Israel’s history?
options: They mark the fulfillment of prophetic judgment against unfaithfulness
They introduce the era of Israel’s monarchy
They describe Israel’s initial conquest of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: They mark the fulfillment of prophetic judgment against unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 describe Nebuchadnezzar’s siege of Jerusalem, fulfilling earlier prophetic warnings about judgment for Israel’s covenant unfaithfulness (2 Kings 25:1-2). This event is pivotal in the biblical narrative of exile and restoration (Jeremiah 25:11-12).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 2 Kings 25:3 and 11 convey about the consequences of sin on a community?
options: Sin leads to both physical suffering and social displacement
Sin results only in spiritual consequences
Sin protects the city from famine
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to both physical suffering and social displacement
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes famine in Jerusalem, while verse 11 recounts the exile of the remaining people, showing that sin brings comprehensive judgment affecting both physical needs and social order (2 Kings 25:3, 11). This aligns with the doctrine of sin’s pervasive effects (Romans 8:20-22).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the Babylonian exile was merely a political event with no spiritual significance. What does 2 Kings 25:4-5 and 21 teach about the spiritual dimension of this event?
options: The exile is a fulfillment of divine judgment for covenant unfaithfulness
It was only a chance political occurrence
It was a myth with no historical basis
It was a sign of God’s approval
questions.correctAnswer: The exile is a fulfillment of divine judgment for covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 describe the king’s flight and capture, and verse 21 records the execution of leaders, showing this event is a direct fulfillment of God’s judgment on unfaithfulness, not merely political (2 Kings 25:4-5, 21). This corresponds with prophetic warnings (Jeremiah 34:17).

questions.question: What theological significance is found in the detailed description of the two brass pillars and their decorations in 2 Kings 25:17?
options: They symbolize the glory and holiness of the temple lost due to Israel’s sin
They are mere architectural details without significance
They symbolize the permanence of Israel’s kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize the glory and holiness of the temple lost due to Israel’s sin
questions.explanation: Verse 17’s detailed description of the pillars with chapiters and pomegranates highlights the temple’s former glory and sanctity, now destroyed due to Israel’s sinfulness and covenant breach (2 Kings 25:17). This loss signifies the gravity of sin against God’s holiness (Exodus 27:1-2).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Kings 25:8 and 9 offer about God’s judgment upon the temple and monarchy?
options: God’s judgment condemns both religious and political institutions when they fail to obey Him
God only judges the kings, sparing the temple
The temple was protected from destruction
God’s judgment is limited to foreign enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment condemns both religious and political institutions when they fail to obey Him
questions.explanation: Verse 8 introduces Nebuzaradan’s arrival, and verse 9 describes the burning of the temple and king’s house, showing that God’s judgment extends to both religious and political leadership due to covenant unfaithfulness (2 Kings 25:8-9). This reflects the seriousness of sin affecting all societal spheres (Psalm 78:60).

questions.question: How do 2 Kings 25:19-21 illustrate the justice of God in dealing with national leaders and officials?
options: God’s justice involves the removal of corrupt leadership to bring about discipline
God ignores the actions of leaders
God always pardons kings and officials
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice involves the removal of corrupt leadership to bring about discipline
questions.explanation: Verses 19-21 describe the capture and execution of leaders and officials, demonstrating God’s just removal of corrupt leadership as discipline for the nation’s sins (2 Kings 25:19-21). This corresponds with biblical principles of leadership responsibility (1 Samuel 2:25).

questions.question: What does the sparing of the poor in 2 Kings 25:12 teach about God's purpose in judgment and restoration?
options: God preserves a remnant for future restoration
God intends complete destruction without hope
God’s judgment is irreversible and final
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a remnant for future restoration
questions.explanation: The captain of the guard leaving some poor to tend vineyards and fields shows God's intention to preserve a remnant to sustain life and enable future restoration (2 Kings 25:12). This reflects the biblical theme of remnant theology (Isaiah 10:20-22).
